newsitem.title: ITALY: Israel's Netanyahu in Rome to meet Pope, Italians.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Netanyahu in Rome to meet Pope, Italians.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu arrived in Rome on Monday for talks with Pope John Paul and Italian leaders.
The visit is Netanyahu's first to Italy since his election last May.
He was due to meet the Pope for an audience at the Vatican before talks with Prime Minister Romano Prodi and Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini later in the day.

Netanyahu arrived in Rome from the World Economic Forum in the Swiss resort of Davos, where he met Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Sunday. They agreed to meet again on Thursday for detailed talks on extending Palestinian self-rule.
Netanyahu told the Rome newspaper Il Messaggero last week that he would discuss the Middle East situation with the Pope, including Jerusalem, which Israel regards as its capital.
"We are ready to give guarantees to Christians and Moslems but we do not intend to discuss the (city's) political sovereignty," Netanyahu was quoted as saying.
The Vatican wants international guarantees protecting the Holy City as sacred to Jews, Christians and Moslems.
Israel captured Arab East Jerusalem, which Palestinians see as their future capital, from Jordan in the 1967 Six-Day War.
Most states including the Vatican do not recognise Israel's 1980 claim to Jerusalem as its "united and eternal capital" and keep their embassies in or near Tel Aviv.
The Vatican and Israel established full diplomatic ties two years ago, ending centuries of often hostile Catholic-Jewish relations.
The Pope and Arafat discussed the Middle East peace process at the Vatican last month.
